newsitem.title: USA: HSBC James Capel cuts Brazil, raises Mexico, Peru.
newsitem.headline: HSBC James Capel cuts Brazil, raises Mexico, Peru.

text.p: HSBC James Capel strategist Ondine Smulders cut Brazil's rating in a model Latin American stock portfolio Tuesday to underweight from overweight.
She also upgraded Mexico and Peru to overweight from neutral. Chile remained overweight.
"We are cutting our weighting in Brazil as there as been a deterioration in the directional drives while the support variables of this market are no longer as strong," she wrote in a report.
She cited interest rates that are no longer dropping, lack of progress on structural reforms and a slowing economy as reasons for the downgrade.
Smulders kept her year-end target for the Bovespa -- Brazil's major stock index -- of 11,000. The exchange was down 45 points to 10,461 early Tuesday.
She upgraded Mexico in part because of improving monetary conditions -- including falling interest rates -- better corporate earnings and the relative cheapness of shares.
"We also are upgrading Peru as better economic performance spells good news for earnings and (President Alberto) Fujimori," Smulders wrote.

She remained overweight in Chile and upgraded her 1997 year-end target for Santiago's IPSA index to 130 from 127 and for the ADRian -- an index of Chilean American Depositary Receipts -- to 1,250 from 1,215. The IPSA was up 0.22 at 121.32.
"We still like Chile as there is further room for interest rate cuts ... while pension funds so far have failed to move on the Central Bank's easing monetary policy," she said.
"In addition, Chile remains our favorite market as a defensive play against the tightening monetary conditions" in the United States.
